description:
CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became: no EXEC PGM=CSUTLDTC exists in app/jcl and the program is CALLed four times by two online programs (CORPT00C L392 and L412, COTRN02C L393 and L413), so it is never a Spring Batch job and is reached here as a plain object, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP layer in the path. LS-DATE='2022-00-15' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-DD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85); LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. The program declares no FILE-CONTROL and no FD, only WORKING-STORAGE (L22) and LINKAGE (L83), so it seeds no dataset, writes no record, leaves no dataset state and takes no job parameter - its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from the thirteen spans of 01 WS-MESSAGE (L42-L57), which sum to exactly 80, and are never captured from a COBOL run: no Language Environment CEE* service exists here, so CEEDAYS cannot be executed. The pinned site is L139-L140, arm 6 of the ten-arm EVALUATE TRUE (L128-L149, WHEN OTHER last): FC-INVALID-MONTH is matched at L139 and moves 'Invalid month  ' at L140, a literal the author had already padded to 15 with two trailing spaces and a lower-case m, reproduced byte for byte rather than stripped and re-padded. Severity 3 and message 2517 are DECODED from the 88-level VALUE X'000309D559C3C5C5' at L67 - the halfwords 0x0003 and 0x09D5 - and never interpolated from the neighbouring arms: 2513 precedes and 2518 follows, so 2514, 2515 and 2516 do not exist. Month 00 is the LOWER out-of-range value and case13 drives the upper one with 13; the pair is what stops a guard written only as 'month > 12', or only as 'month < 1', from passing. 00 is numeric and fills its field, so nothing about the text's SHAPE is wrong - that is what separates 2517 from 2520 FC-NON-NUMERIC-DATA - and the month is rejected before the day is ever measured against a month length, which separates it from 2508 FC-BAD-DATE-VALUE, where the month is valid and only the day is impossible. The TstDate span carries an expected corruption, not a defect to repair: L105 moves LENGTH OF LS-DATE, always the declared 10, into the S9(4) BINARY Vstring-length, and the group move at L122 then overwrites the clean date L107 had placed in WS-DATE with the leftmost ten bytes of WS-DATE-TO-TEST, so WS-DATE receives the halfword 0x00 0x0A and only the first eight characters. Here the offending month digits survive that truncation, where in case07 the offending day fell off the end. WS-DATE-FMT is set once at L111-L113 before the CALL and L122 targets WS-DATE alone, so the mask span stays clean.

THE TWO CALL PARAMETERS, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. unitStimulus.linkage carries this case's whole input: LS-DATE = '2022-00-15' and LS-DATE-FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD', each written out to the ten characters PIC X(10) declares at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:84-85 with every trailing space visible - a mask longer than ten characters is TRUNCATED by the receiving field, and the truncation changes the message number, so the width has to be readable at the point the value is written. CSUTLDTC seeds no dataset and drives no screen, so these two values are the only thing a case varies; they used to live in a table in CSUTLDTCParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', which meant this file stated an eighty-byte result with nothing in it to say what was validated, and cases that differ only in their input were indistinguishable on disk.
